items.titleEn: Why is Disney planning thousands of job cuts despite double-digit earnings forecast?
items.summaryEn: Buy Walt Disney (DIS). The article shows management is extending a proven cost-cutting playbook (prior restructurings) while still projecting double-digit adjusted EPS growth. Parks/cruises are already profitable, and streaming margins are ~13%—so incremental savings should flow to operating leverage and fund higher-return investments (Disney+ tech/content, Hulu integration). Key Risk: They cut the wrong costs (creative/tech/guest-facing), damaging franchises and subscriber growth so margins don’t expand. Sell Netflix (NFLX). Disney is signaling a clearer path to durable double-digit Disney+ profit growth via cost discipline and operating leverage, plus Hulu/Disney+ integration. If Disney’s streaming margins keep rising, it pressures Netflix’s ability to grow profits without matching spend, especially as Disney reinvests selectively rather than broadly.

items.titleEn: Why did South Korea's KOSPI erase Monday's 2.2% rally in one session?
items.summaryEn: Buy KOSPI exposure (e.g., iShares MSCI South Korea ETF, EWY). Monday’s rally was driven by domestic institutions; Tuesday’s drop shows that support is withdrawing, but the index is now near 5,700 where valuation support and improving semis earnings forecasts are pulling multiples toward historically low levels. Retail dip-buying is already showing up, so the next move is likely a stabilization bounce if foreign selling slows into the US midterm results. Key Risk: Foreign investors keep selling aggressively after the US election, overwhelming valuation support and pushing KOSPI below 5,700. Buy Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) and SK Hynix (000660.KS). The sell-off is being driven by US AI spending fears that hit US tech first, then spread to Korean memory and AI-adjacent names. With multiples pushed toward historically low levels and earnings forecasts improving, the market is likely over-discounting near-term AI capex uncertainty.

items.titleEn: Samsung and SK Hynix stocks plunge as a $20 billion AI shock rattles markets
items.summaryEn: SK Hynix has stronger downside protection from long-term supply agreements covering more than half of 2027–28 capacity, plus ongoing HBM4 and server-memory momentum. If customers become cautious, contracts and HBM stickiness should cushion volumes and pricing better than for peers. Buy 000660.KS on weakness; focus on the next 1–3 quarters as sentiment stabilizes. Key Risk: Customers renegotiate or delay HBM/server-memory orders despite existing agreements. Oracle’s $20B raise signals Big Tech may need more external funding to keep AI buildouts accelerating. That raises the odds of slower, more selective memory purchases and margin pressure at the next cycle turn. Samsung is the more valuation-sensitive name here (Korea Investment cut its target sharply), so the stock can stay weak even if profits are still strong. Sell/short 005930.KS into any bounce; pair with a smaller hedge in the sector if needed.

items.titleEn: Apple posts earnings beat with better than expected iPhone and Mac sales
items.summaryEn: Buy Apple (AAPL). Earnings beat plus iPhone and Mac outperformance, with Services at $31.6B and gross margin holding at 47.9%, signals resilient demand and pricing power despite component shortages. Market share rising (18%→22%) while the smartphone market shrinks supports share-gain, not just a one-off quarter. Key risk: Holiday guidance disappoints because supply constraints and iPhone Duo delays cut sell-through enough to outweigh the pricing benefit. Key Risk: Holiday outlook/guidance breaks—iPhone supply and Duo delays cause demand to fall faster than Apple can ship. Buy Micron (MU) and/or SK hynix ADR (if available to you). Apple’s iPhone price hikes and supply limits are tied to memory-chip scarcity; when a mega-cap customer reports strong results despite shortages, it usually means the memory bottleneck is easing or being allocated profitably. That lifts pricing and utilization for memory suppliers. Key risk: Memory demand weakens broadly (not just Apple), forcing prices down and wiping out the scarcity premium.

items.titleEn: Palantir delivers blowout quarter - but there's a catch
items.summaryEn: Buy Palantir (PLTR). The quarter shows corporate AI spending is translating into real revenue, and commercial revenue is now the biggest slice. The key is that management’s Q4 outlook still implies strong sequential growth, so the market’s “replenishment” worry can be answered if bookings catch up over the next few quarters. You’re buying the probability-weighted path where commercial deployments deepen and revenue keeps compounding. Key Risk: New US commercial contract signings stay weak for multiple quarters, so revenue growth is just converting older deals and the valuation can’t be supported. Sell Palantir (PLTR) if the next earnings cycle confirms the gap: US commercial revenue up sharply while new US commercial contract value remains near-flat. That pattern means customers are buying work already in motion, not expanding commitments. If guidance holds but bookings don’t, the stock rerates lower because the market stops believing in sustained growth.
